title: Google revamps European search results under DMA compliance after €890 million EU antitrust fine
summary: Google has warned users in the European Economic Area that it will modify its site reputation abuse policy for Search, months after the European Commission fined the company €890 million in July for Digital Markets Act breaches on Google Search self-preferencing and Play steering. The ITIF Foundation noted on 3 September that the change shows the recurring cost of DMA compliance for US platforms. The Commission has given Google 60 days to comply or face penalty payments of up to 5 percent of worldwide daily turnover; Google told users its EEA results would be 'lower quality' as a consequence.
